headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: oh-my-openagent’s broad egress and MCP hooks can expose cognee’s sensitive support data if paired without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: oh-my-openagent uses runtime-injected MCPs and hooks, and cognee processes documents and workflows in session memory. If cognee outputs are bridged into those hooks or shared files, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF cognee outputs are copied into an MCP hook or shared file consumed by oh-my-openagent
IF oh-my-openagent parses external content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of cognee outputs into hooks
Add a manual review step before any MCP action
Restrict hooks to allowlisted commands only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while oh-my-openagent has broad network egress and sends data to PostHog, Exa, Context7, and Grep.app. In a shared workspace or copied-output workflow, sensitive cognee content can leave the environment through oh-my-openagent by default. The pairwise leakage path is plausible and the blast radius is large.
conditions: IF cognee data is placed in a workspace or prompt that oh-my-openagent can read
IF oh-my-openagent forwards that content to any external API or telemetry endpoint
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Remove sensitive fields before passing text to oh-my-openagent
Disable telemetry and external search APIs for sensitive runs
Use a local-only proxy for any required lookups
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: cognee supports multiple instances with session memory, and oh-my-openagent supports multiple instances with per-installation scope plus full-permissions mode. Their write surfaces differ, but both can mutate local state and invoke tools, so overlapping access to the same installation or workspace can create conflicts. The exact shared target is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace, config, or cache directory
IF oh-my-openagent runs in full-permissions mode while cognee is active on the same files
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Avoid concurrent runs on the same project tree
Serialize writes with a simple operator checklist
Lock shared config files during edits
requires-engineering: add filesystem locking or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: oh-my-openagent exposes task and message APIs plus LSP actions, so it can act on upstream text. cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations that could be treated as authoritative inputs. If cognee output is fed into oh-my-openagent without verification, errors can cascade into edits or messages. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF cognee output is used as input to oh-my-openagent task or message APIs
IF oh-my-openagent executes LSP or subprocess actions without a verification step
mitigations: Require human approval before actions
Add a validation checklist for cognee-derived claims
Limit oh-my-openagent to read-only tasks for first pass
Log source-to-action links for review
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating before execution

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while oh-my-openagent handles provider authentication data and sends telemetry to third parties. If the pair processes regulated or sensitive support records together, retention, residency, and third-party transfer obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF personal data or finance data from cognee is routed through oh-my-openagent
IF telemetry or external APIs receive regulated content
mitigations: Exclude regulated records from oh-my-openagent runs
Review telemetry settings before processing sensitive data
Keep a short operator note on data residency assumptions
Delete transient logs after each session
requires-engineering: align retention and DPA controls across both agents
